newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Weaker on soft crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Weaker on soft crude.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps slipped at midday on Monday amid weaker crude values and lacklustre talks, brokers said.
May gas oil swaps were last quoted $25.00/$25.25 per barrel, down from Friday's quotes at $25.05/$25.15.
On Friday, Brent crude levels on London's International Petroleum Exchange fell to a session low of $17.88 per barrel, easing 32 cents.
At midday SIMEX Brent remained unquoted, providing little direction. The West Texas Intermediate June contract on ACCESS was down one cent at $19.60 per barrel.

Brokers said the gas oil market was expected to see some downward pressure following results of the latest Indian tender. India bought around 270,000 tonnes for June delivery, well below traders expectations of 600,000 tonnes.
Traders said the market is also shrouded by uncertainties on whether or not two Singapore traders have completed by purchases.
Hin Leong Trading, together with two other traders, have since March 3 bought over 18 million barrels of physical gas oil.
While some of the oil were expected to be placed into the bunker market, Indonesia and China, most traders were still uncertain whether these outlets could absorb all the oil that had been purchased.
"I do not think these outlets are able to take in all the supplies, taking into consideration, China would also have imported some of its oil from South Korea," one trader said.
Fuel oil swaps were also lower, with May seen at $98.00/$99.00, brokers said.
